java.fixed_code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){int x = 10; double y = x / 3.0;}}

java.code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){String s = "hello"; char c = s.charAt(10);}}
java.explanation: String index 10 is out of bounds for length 5.
java.fixed_code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){String s = "hello"; char c = s.charAt(4);}}

java.code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){int[] arr = null; System.out.println(arr.length);}}
java.explanation: Cannot access length of null array.
java.fixed_code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){int[] arr = new int[5]; System.out.println(arr.length);}}

java.code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){List<Integer> list = null; list.add(5);}}
java.explanation: Cannot call methods on a null List reference.
java.fixed_code: public class Main{public static void main(String[] args){List<Integer> list = new ArrayList<>(); list.add(5);}}

java.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[ args){ System.out.println("Hello, World!"); } }
java.error:
Main.java:1: error: ']' expected
public class Main { public static void main(String[ args){ System.out.println("Hello, World!"); } }
                                                   ^
1 error
java.explanation:
The error message `error: ']' expected` is quite specific and points directly to the problem.

### Explanation of the Error

In Java, when you declare an array type, you need to use a pair of square brackets `[]` to indicate it's an array. In the `main` method signature, `String[ args` is supposed to declare `args` as an array of `String` objects. However, it's missing the closing square bracket. It should be `String[] args` to correctly specify that `args` is an array of `String`
java.fixed_code: public class Main { public static void main(String[ args){ System.out.println("Hello, World!"); } }
